The wobble board is an idiophone invented and popularised by the Australian musician and artist Rolf Harris, and heard on his best-known song 'Tie Me Kangaroo Down, Sport'. It is a large, flexible sheet with a shallow hollow in the middle of one short edge for the palm to grip; the player holds the sheet with the palm or the edge of the hand and springs it outwards, which makes a whirring sound, and the angle of the sheet and the way it is sprung change the timbre. It is close to the thunder sheet, the metal instrument that eighteenth-century theatre used to imitate thunder, and players can also make one from hardboard and other materials.
搖晃板由澳洲音樂家與藝術家 Rolf Harris 發明並普及，亦見於其歌曲「T: The wobble board was invented and popularised by the Australian musician and artist Rolf Harris, and appears in his song 'Tie Me Kangaroo Down, Sport'. In a 2001 interview Harris said that in 1959, while preparing to paint a portrait of the magician Robert Harbin, the oil paint on a hardboard was still wet and he dried it over a paraffin heater; when it was too hot to hold he gripped the board between his palms and wobbled it, and found the sound by accident. Official Rolf Harris wobble boards were sold in the 1970s, but most are made by players themselves; any large flexible sheet can be used ad hoc. Two boards donated by Harris were held by the National Museum of Australia, and were removed in 2013 after his arrest on indecent assault charges.
搖晃板發出的聲音具有獨特的低頻「嗚嗚」音，音色沉著而富有共鳴感，帶有明顯的原始與: The wobble board makes a distinctive low whirring sound, steady and resonant, with an obviously raw, folk quality. Its range lies mainly in the low and lower-middle register; the volume does not stand out but it carries well. When both hands spring the board quickly, the board itself resonates naturally and makes a rhythmic undulation of sound. The sound resembles the low hum of wind through a valley, between the dry attack of percussion and the sustained tone of a wind instrument. Compared with the clear strike of a drum it is more fluid; compared with string instruments its timbre is heavier and more raw. That makes it a good instrument for atmosphere, especially for images of nature and wilderness.

演奏搖晃板時，雙手沿長邊握住板緣，將板向外甩動，發出呼呼聲；持板角度與甩動方式會: To play the wobble board, hold it by the long edges and spring it outwards, which makes a whooshing sound; the angle and the way you spring it change the timbre. A beginner should let the board bounce between the two palms rather than gripping it with the fingers; the shallow hollow in the middle of one short edge, about a palm wide and a quarter of an inch deep, keeps the hand from slipping. In practice, accent every second beat and do not spring on every beat. Thin hardboard or thin MDF springs more easily; too thick a sheet is hard to work.
